summary: Amalananda Ghosh (1910–1981) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at University College London (~1937–1938). He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1937–1968) and Fellow at the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1968–1971).
Amalia Pezzali (born 1928) is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She studied under Olivier Lacombe, Michel Hulin, and as a doctoral student under T. R. V. Murti.

Amanda K. Goodman is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. She earned her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, supervised by Robert H. Sharf, Luis Oscar Gómez, and Donald S. Lopez Jr., and holds a teaching position at the University of Toronto.
Amar Nath Pandeya worked in the fields of Indology and philosophy. He held posts at the University of Delhi (attested 1968) and Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (attested 1987).

Amar Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He completed doctoral studies under Anthony Kennedy Warder (attested 1984) and was taught by Rahul Sankrityayan (1960–1963), Bimal Krishna Matilal, T. Venkatacharya, Shoryu Katsura, Masafumi Fujimoto, and Alasdair Urquhart.

Amara Ali is an Indology and linguistics scholar. In 2026, she held attested posts as a Lecturer in Urdu at both the University of California, Berkeley, and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.

Amaranatha Jha (1897–1955) earned a B.A. from Muir Central College (~1913–1917), where he became Professor of English in 1917. He later served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Allahabad (~1938–1946) and Banaras Hindu University (~1947–1948).
Amarasvar Thakur was an Indology scholar who held a post at the University of Calcutta (attested 1936) and served as General Editor of the Calcutta Sanskrit Series.

Amartya Sen (born 1933) is a philosopher and economist who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1951–1953) and Cambridge (~1953–1959). He held positions at Jadavpur, Delhi, LSE, Calcutta, and Harvard, where he was appointed Thomas W. Lamont University Professor around 2004.

Amaury de Riencourt (1918–2005) was a scholar in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the Sorbonne and University of Paris (~1936–1937) and earned an M.A. at the University of Algiers (~1937–1939).
Amba Kulkarni works in computational linguistics and Indology. She completed her Ph.D. in 2009 at the University of Hyderabad, where she serves as a professor (attested 2018–2026).

Amber D. Carpenter specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied under M. M. McCabe, Verity Harte, Raimond Gaita, Jonathan Lear, Susan Neiman, and Jonathan Glover. Her academic posts include Yale-NUS College, University of St Andrews, and University of York.

Ambrogio Ballini (1879–1950) was an Indologist who studied at Padua, Bologna, and Bonn under scholars including Teza, Pullè, Formichi, and Jacobi. He held ordinary professorships of Sanskrit at Padua (1913), Università Cattolica (1924), and Sapienza University of Rome (1941–1949).

Amelia Bonea (born 1978) is a historian of science, technology, medicine, and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo and Heidelberg University (PhD 2012). She held posts at Oxford and Heidelberg before becoming Senior Lecturer at the University of Manchester (~2020).

Amelia Hall is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her doctorate at the University of Oxford in 2012. Her appointments include Assistant Professor of IndoTibetan Buddhism at Naropa University and online faculty at Central Michigan University (attested 2019).

Ameneh Shirazinejad is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She has held posts as an Arabic language tutor at George Washington University and as a Visiting Fellow at the University of Delhi.

Amin Sweeney (1938–2010) was a linguist who earned his doctorate at the University of London (~1967–1970). He taught at the National University of Malaysia (1970–1977) and UC Berkeley, where he chaired the South and Southeast Asian Studies Department (1986–1991).
Amita Chatterjee (born 1950) is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who served as a professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University (attested 1999 and 2009).
Amod Jayant Lele is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Parimal G. Patil.

Amrit Madhav Ghatage (1913–2003) was an Indologist and linguist. He was Professor and Head of Linguistics at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1961–1978) and later served as Vice-President of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1993–2003).
